The title of this project is the FY29 AFRL Systems & Digital Engineering Laboratory  Project Number MHMV203102  Kirtland Air Force Base  New Mexico.  Its purpose is to design and construct a new two-story 150 000 SF (13 936 SM) laboratory  including the demolition of thirteen (13) buildings  totaling 122 837 SF. This primary facility will design and construct the laboratory with a reinforced concrete foundation and structural slab  structural steel frame  insulated metal panel exterior walls and storefront windows. The new spacecraft lab facility includes spacecraft cleanrooms  an electronics lab  caged storage  supporting mission operation function  administrative spaces  and typical circulation spaces. The facility will include both controlled unclassified spaces and secure spaces compliant with ICD/ICS 705 standards. The supporting exterior improvements include a secure exterior concrete testing yard and loading dock  an asphalt parking lot (126 spaces)  sidewalks  exterior site concrete  equipment pads  and electrical/mechanical yards.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The proposed building is located north of the Albuquerque International Sunport airport and within the northwest boundary of Kirtland Air Force Base. The structure is bounded by Aberdeen Ave at the south and Charlene Drive at the east.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION:
The proposed project involves the reconstruction of the existing bridge along Minnesota Avenue over a drainage ditch  just south of Norton Drive. The permanent bridge structure will not be elevated any higher than the existing bridge which crosses the existing ditch at the same elevation as the adjacent roadway. Basically flat.

During construction  drilling rigs will be used to excavate for the bridge foundations.  These rigs will be approximately 80ft tall.  Also  cranes will be used to lift steel reinforcing cages into the drilled holes. These cranes will also be approximately 80ft tall.  Also cranes will be used to lift precast bridge girders into place.  These cranes will be approximately 50ft tall. 

The proposed construction will occur over a period of 8 months  however  the drilling equipment and cranes used to lift reinforcing cages will likely occur over the period of 1 month.  Similarly the lifting and hanging of the bridge girders will last another month.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The Texas Department of Transportation will be constructing the extension of SL 390 from US80 passing through Elysian Fields Rd and connecting to IH-20. High mast illumination poles are recommended especially at the interchanges and at the entrance/exit ramps. Due to the close proximity of Elysian Fields Rd to Harrison County Airport  30 ft and 50 ft illumination poles are designed to cover that future roundabout and exit/entrance ramps in close proximity to the airport. The project will include twenty-nine (29) additional high mast illumination poles. Fourteen (20) safety lighting poles of 50 ft height are designed to cover Elysian Fields Rd roundabout entrance/exit ramp north of the proposed bridge. Six (6) standard light poles of 30 ft height to cover the entrance/exit ramps south of the bridge leading to Elysian Fields Rd.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: Standard lighting poles to be placed at the entrance and exit ramps of the future bridge crossing creek
